record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop a broader theory of random matrices with non-independent coefficients, especially matrices constrained by geometric structure, so that random-matrix methods become usable in higher-dimensional constructive problems.

evidence.quote: An important progress may come from the understanding of random matrices with non-independent coefficients... Constructivists... may therefore try to develop a more general theory of random matrices, including in particular those with constraints of geometric origin

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a general theory of random matrices whose entries are not independent, with particular emphasis on ensembles whose laws are constrained by an underlying geometric structure (for example, matrices whose entries are indexed by simplices, cells, or faces of a simplicial complex or CW-complex, with joint distributions reflecting incidence, locality, or symmetry constraints, rather than i.i.d. or Wigner-type independence assumptions).

Concretely, the goal is to:

1. Identify natural classes of probability measures on spaces of N×N (or rectangular) real/complex/Hermitian matrices M = (M_{ij}) whose entries satisfy explicit dependence relations coming from a geometric or combinatorial structure G (e.g. M_{ij} ≠ 0 only when i,j share a face, or entries are functions of underlying random tensors of higher rank indexed by G).

2. For such ensembles, establish quantitative non-asymptotic bounds on the operator norm ‖M‖ and on the smallest singular value, together with concentration inequalities for linear statistics tr f(M), as functions of N, the geometric data of G, and the marginal distributions of the entries.

3. Determine the limiting spectral distribution (analogue of the Wigner semicircle / Marchenko–Pastur law) for natural families of such geometrically constrained ensembles as N → ∞, and characterize universality classes.

4. Provide moment and cumulant bounds sharp enough that the resulting estimates can be applied uniformly across families indexed by a geometric parameter (e.g. dimension d of the underlying complex), in particular yielding bounds whose dependence on d is explicit and controlled.

The problem is to build such a theory, prove the corresponding spectral and norm estimates, and exhibit nontrivial classes of geometrically constrained random matrix ensembles for which all of the above can be carried out.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad research program rather than a single precise conjecture. While substantial progress has been made on random matrices with dependent entries (e.g. matrices with given variance profile, sparse/structured Wigner matrices, random tensors and their unfoldings, log-gases with external structure), a comprehensive theory addressing matrices with general geometric constraints remains open and is an active area; no source claims the program is solved.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies of random matrices with correlated/structured entries continue to appear, indicating the theory is still under development.
status_evidence.claim: The general theory of random matrices with geometrically constrained, non-independent entries is still being developed.
